title: Exposing JDownloader’s unauthenticated deprecated API may enable unauthorized queue control
description: JDSH documents enabling the deprecated Local API and notes that localhost-only mode may need to be disabled for remote use. JDownloader’s project manager states that this API has no authentication or encryption by default (https://board.jdownloader.org/showthread.php?p=547625). JDSH connects to the configured host and exposes queue operations. Whether a lower-trust principal can reach the deployed listener through its bind, firewall, VPN, or routing configuration is not established by repository source.
claimed_root_cause: Remote-use setup guidance does not explain that the deprecated API is unauthenticated and unencrypted by default or require restricting its network exposure.

trace.description: Documentation says localhost-only mode may need to be disabled for remote use.
JDSH reads the configured host and port, defaulting to loopback.
JDSH connects directly to the configured JDownloader endpoint; security depends on that endpoint’s network exposure.

evidence.description: Remote use may require setting deprecatedapilocalhostonly to false.
Connection uses configurable host and port; this repository does not implement an authentication check.
Queue and download-controller actions can change local state.

blockers: Whether the deployed listener and network policy make the unauthenticated API reachable by a lower-trust principal is not visible in repository source.

validation_plan.deployment: On the actual deployment configuration, verify listener bind address, firewall/VPN/SSH tunnel rules, and whether any untrusted network can reach the port. Use an isolated staging instance and a dummy queue if an active check is needed; do not probe production.
validation_plan.local: Confirm the deployed JDownloader version’s deprecated API settings and ensure remote access is restricted to explicitly trusted hosts.
